q: How many months of the year have 28 days?
note: Even the shortest month has 28 days, so every month qualifies.

q: In a race, you overtake the runner in second place. What position are you in now?
note: You take their spot, not the leader's; first place is still ahead of you.

q: In a 100 m sprint, you overtake the runner in last place. What position are you in now?
a: Impossible, nobody is behind last place
options: Impossible, nobody is behind last place
note: To pass the last runner you'd have to be behind them, which would make you last.

q: A cockerel lays an egg right on the peak of a tin roof in a village. Which side does the egg roll down?
options: The side the wind blows towards
note: Only hens lay eggs; a cockerel is a male bird.

q: An electric suburban train in Mumbai speeds north while a strong wind blows south. Which way does the train's smoke blow?
note: Electric trains draw power from overhead wires, so there's no smoke to blow anywhere.

q: How much soil is there in a hole exactly 1 metre deep, 1 metre wide and 1 metre long?
note: A hole is empty space; the soil has already been dug out of it.

q: A courier in Mumbai sets out with 30 packages and delivers all but 8. How many packages does he still have?
note: 'All but 8' means every package except 8 was delivered.

q: Divide 30 by half, then add 10. What do you get?
note: Dividing by a half doubles a number: 30 ÷ 0.5 = 60, and 60 + 10 = 70.

q: Your mum hands you 3 biscuits and says: eat one right now, then one every half hour. How many minutes until all 3 are eaten?
note: The first goes at 0 minutes, the second at 30 and the third at 60.

q: Priya's parents have four daughters. Three of them are Suman, Sunita and Sulekha. What is the fourth daughter's name?
note: The question names Priya at the very start; she is the fourth daughter.

q: A bat and a ball cost ₹110 in total. The bat costs ₹100 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
note: If the ball cost ₹10, the bat would be ₹110 and the total ₹120. Ball ₹5, bat ₹105.

q: Water hyacinth on a pond doubles its area every day. It covers the whole pond on day 30. On which day was the pond half covered?
note: Doubling from half to full takes just one day, so it was half covered the day before.

q: If 5 chaiwalas take 5 minutes to make 5 cups of chai, how many minutes would 100 chaiwalas take to make 100 cups?
note: Each chaiwala makes one cup in 5 minutes, however many of them are working.

q: There are 10 mangoes in a basket and you take away 3. How many mangoes do you have?
note: You took 3, so you have 3; the basket is the one left with 7.

q: Which of these is true: 'The yolk of an egg are white' or 'The yolk of an egg is white'?
note: The grammar is a distraction: the white of an egg is the albumen, never the yolk.

q: The Rajdhani leaves Delhi for Mumbai at 120 km/h. At the same moment a slower train leaves Mumbai for Delhi at 80 km/h. When they meet, which is closer to Mumbai?
a: Neither, they're at the same spot
options: Neither, they're at the same spot
It depends on the time of day
note: When two trains meet they're in the same place, so both are equally far from Mumbai.

q: A 1-km-long goods train enters a 1-km tunnel at 60 km/h. How many minutes from the engine entering until the last wagon comes out?
note: The engine must cover 2 km, the tunnel plus the train's own length, at 1 km a minute.

q: An auto driver goes the wrong way down a one-way street, right past a traffic policeman, who does nothing. Why?
options: The auto had a special permit
The street was closed for repairs
note: Nobody said he was in his auto; he was simply on foot.

q: A woman in Pune marries dozens of people every month, all perfectly legally. How?
a: She's a registrar who conducts weddings
options: She marries them in different countries
She's a registrar who conducts weddings
Each wedding lasts only a day
note: To 'marry' a couple can also mean to conduct their wedding.

q: Two fathers and two sons go to the movies and buy exactly three tickets, one each. How?
a: They're a grandad, a dad and a son
options: One of them is a baby who goes free
They're a grandad, a dad and a son
Two of them shared a ticket
note: The middle man is both a father and a son, so three people fill all four roles.

q: Quick: spell S-I-L-K out loud three times. Now, what do cows drink?
note: The rhyme pushes you towards 'milk', but grown cows drink water; milk is for calves.

q: You walk into a dark storeroom with a lantern, a gas stove and a pile of firewood, and you have one matchstick. What do you light first?
note: Nothing else can be lit until the match itself is burning.

q: Can you jump higher than a ten-storey building?
note: A building never leaves the ground, so any hop at all beats it.

q: Ananya turned 20 in 2024, yet she has had only 5 real birthdays. How?
options: She was born just after midnight
note: Born on 29 February 2004, her date only came round in 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024.

q: Two babies are born at exactly the same moment, yet their birth certificates show different dates. How?
a: They were born in different time zones
options: One was born in a taxi
They were born in different time zones
note: Just before midnight in one country, it can already be the next day a few time zones east.

q: Riya and Diya have the same mother and were born on the same day of the same year, but they are not twins. How?
a: They are two of a set of triplets
options: They are two of a set of triplets
They were born in different cities
Their birthdays are a year apart
note: Triplets share a mother and a birthday, so any two of them aren't twins.

q: A man asks a chai-stall owner for a glass of water. The owner suddenly shouts 'BOO!' right behind him. The man thanks him and leaves. Why?
options: He had come to ask for directions
He had asked for chai instead
note: A sudden fright is a folk cure for hiccups, which is also why he asked for water.

q: Raju rode into the village on Friday, stayed three nights and rode out on Friday. How?
options: He rode through the night each time
The village uses a different calendar
note: Friday is the horse he rode, not the day he arrived.

q: How far can a deer run into a forest?
note: After the halfway point it is running out of the forest, not into it.

q: At a wedding, Pintu eats 10 gulab jamuns on an empty stomach. How many did he eat on an empty stomach?
note: After the first gulab jamun, his stomach wasn't empty any more.

q: A small town has only two hairdressers. One has a neat haircut; the other's hair is a mess. Who should you go to?
a: The one with the messy hair
options: The one with the neat haircut
The one with the messy hair
note: Neither can cut their own hair well, so each one's haircut is the other's work.

q: Why are 2010 one-rupee coins worth more than 2009 one-rupee coins?
note: Read it as 2,010 coins against 2,009 coins: one extra rupee.

q: An ant, a cat and a lizard race to the top of a pine tree. Who gets the mango first?
a: Nobody, pine trees don't grow mangoes
options: Nobody, pine trees don't grow mangoes
note: Pine trees bear cones; mangoes grow on a completely different tree.

q: A driver with no headlights, on a village road with no streetlights and no moon, stops just in time for a black cow. How did he see it?
note: Nobody said it was night; streetlights and the moon don't matter at noon.

q: With nobody touching it, nothing tied to it and nothing for it to hit, how can you throw a cricket ball as hard as you can and have it come back to you?
note: What goes up comes back down, straight into your hands.

q: A cow is tied to a 5-metre rope. A patch of grass is 10 metres away, yet the cow reaches it easily. How?
a: The rope isn't tied to anything
options: The rope isn't tied to anything
The cow walks in a spiral
note: The cow is tied to the rope, but nobody said the rope was tied to a post.

q: A tempo gets wedged under a low railway bridge, just 2 cm too tall to pass. How can the driver free it without damaging anything?
a: Let some air out of the tyres
options: Hose the roof with cold water
Let some air out of the tyres
note: Softer tyres lower the tempo slightly; unloading would let its springs lift it higher.

q: A boat moored at Kochi has a rope ladder over its side with 3 rungs underwater. The tide rises 1 metre. How many rungs are underwater now?
note: The boat floats, so it rises with the tide and the ladder rises with it.

q: Meena drops her ring into a full cup of chai, pulls it out, and the ring is completely dry. How?
a: The cup was full of dry tea leaves
options: The cup was full of dry tea leaves
note: A cup full of dry chai patti still counts as a full cup of chai, just not brewed.

q: How can someone go eight days without sleeping?
note: They skip sleeping during the day; nobody said they stayed awake at night.

q: A fan in Chennai claims he can tell you the score of any cricket match before it starts, every single time. How?
a: Before it starts, the score is 0 for 0
options: Before it starts, the score is 0 for 0
He has a friend in the dressing room
note: Before a ball is bowled, every team is on zero runs for zero wickets.

q: Two days ago Aman was 19. Next year he will turn 22. How is that possible?
a: Today is 1 January and his birthday is 31 December
options: He had two birthdays in one year
He lied about his age once
Today is 1 January and his birthday is 31 December
He counts birthdays on another calendar
note: On 30 December he was 19, turned 20 on the 31st, turns 21 this year and 22 next year.

q: When Rahul was 6, his neighbour Tina was half his age. Rahul is now 40. How old is Tina?
note: She was 3 when he was 6, so she is always 3 years younger.

q: A captain has lost the toss 9 times in a row with a fair coin. What is the chance he wins the next toss?
note: A coin has no memory; every fair toss is still a 50-50 call.

q: On a game show you pick 1 of 3 doors: a car behind one, goats behind two. The host, who knows where the car is, always opens another door showing a goat and offers a switch. Should you switch?
note: Sticking wins 1 time in 3; switching wins 2 times in 3.

q: Rahul buys a cycle for ₹6,000, sells it for ₹7,000, buys it back for ₹8,000 and sells it again for ₹9,000. What is his total profit?
note: He paid ₹14,000 in all and received ₹16,000, so he is ₹2,000 ahead.

q: Three friends pay ₹3,000 for a Goa room. The manager refunds ₹500; the bellboy keeps ₹200 and returns ₹100 each. So each paid ₹900: ₹2,700 plus ₹200 is ₹2,900. Where's the missing ₹100?
a: There's none; the ₹200 is inside the ₹2,700
options: There's none; the ₹200 is inside the ₹2,700
note: ₹2,700 paid = ₹2,500 room + ₹200 bellboy. Add the ₹300 refunded and you're back to ₹3,000.

q: A hen and a half lays an egg and a half in a day and a half. How many eggs does one hen lay in one day?
note: One hen lays one egg in a day and a half, so 2/3 of an egg per day.

q: You drive up to a hill station at 30 km/h and come back down the same road at 60 km/h. What is your average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
note: Say it's 60 km each way: the 120 km round trip takes 3 hours, which is 40 km/h.

q: A rope fits snugly around Earth's equator. Roughly how much longer must it be to hover 1 metre above the ground all the way round?
note: The extra length is 2π × 1 metre, whether you wrap a ball or a whole planet.

q: A brick weighs 1 kg plus half a brick. How much does one whole brick weigh?
note: If half a brick weighs 1 kg, the whole brick must weigh 2 kg.

q: A 100-metre road has a lamp post at each end and one every 10 metres in between. How many lamp posts are there?
note: Ten 10-metre gaps need one more post than there are gaps, counting both ends.

q: Climbing from the 1st floor to the 3rd floor takes 1 minute. At the same pace, how long does it take to climb from the 1st floor to the 6th floor?
note: 1st to 3rd is 2 flights; 1st to 6th is 5 flights, so it takes 2.5 times as long.

q: Add these in your head: 1000 + 40 + 1000 + 30 + 1000 + 20 + 1000 + 10. What is the total?
note: Many people blurt out 5000; the tens add up to 100, not 1000.

q: Quick, no calculator: what is 3 + 3 × 3?
note: Multiplication comes first: 3 × 3 = 9, then 3 + 9 = 12.

q: How many letters are there in the answer to this question?
note: 'Four' has four letters, the only English number word that matches its own letter count.

q: Rearrange the letters of NEW DOOR to make one word.
note: N-E-W-D-O-O-R rearranges into O-N-E-W-O-R-D, literally 'one word'.

q: Which 11-letter English word is misspelled in every dictionary?
note: Every dictionary spells the word 'incorrectly' as i-n-c-o-r-r-e-c-t-l-y.

q: What is unusual about the number 8,549,176,320?
a: Its digits are in alphabetical order in English
options: Its digits are in alphabetical order in English
note: Eight, five, four, nine, one, seven, six, three, two, zero: A to Z.

q: What happened in 1961 that won't happen again until the year 6009?
a: It reads the same after a half-turn rotation
options: It reads the same after a half-turn rotation
note: Rotate 1961 by half a turn and it still reads 1961; 6009 is the next year that does.

q: Count the letter F in this sentence: THE FILES OF THE FIRM ARE FULL OF FACTS
note: Most people skip the Fs in 'OF', because they sound like a V.

q: Which side of a chai cup is the handle on?
note: People say left or right, but that depends on how you hold it; it's always on the outside.

q: How can you drop a raw egg onto a concrete floor without cracking the concrete?
a: Just drop it, an egg can't crack concrete
options: Just drop it, an egg can't crack concrete
note: The egg will smash, but the floor will be perfectly fine.

q: How many ends do three and a half sticks have?
note: Half a stick is still a stick with two ends: 3 × 2 + 2 = 8.

q: You have two notes that add up to ₹30, and one of them is not a ₹10 note. What are they?
note: The ₹20 is the one that isn't a ₹10 note; the other one is.

q: With an old wind-up alarm clock, you go to bed at 8 pm and set the alarm for 9 o'clock. How many hours of sleep do you get before it rings?
note: A wind-up clock has no am or pm, so it rings at 9 pm.

q: Is there a 26th of January in America?
note: Every calendar has a 26 January; it just isn't a holiday there.

q: Verma ji's son topped his class exam and also got the lowest marks in the class. How?
a: He was the only student who took it
options: The topper was chosen by attendance
He was the only student who took it
Marks were counted from the bottom
note: With one student sitting the exam, the top score and the bottom score are the same.

q: Volumes 1 and 2 of an English encyclopedia stand in order on a shelf, spines facing you. Each has 5 cm of pages and 2 mm covers. A bookworm bores from page 1 of Volume 1 to the last page of Volume 2. How far?
note: Page 1 of Volume 1 sits right next to Volume 2's last page, with only two covers between.

q: A 60-page weekend paper is made of large sheets folded in half. Pages 7 and 8 are printed on one half of a sheet. Which pages are on the other half of that sheet?
note: Pages sharing a sheet add up to 61: 7 pairs with 54, and 8 with 53.

q: A painter slips off a 6-metre ladder onto a concrete floor but doesn't get a scratch. How?
a: He was on the bottom rung
options: He was on the bottom rung
note: From the lowest rung, 'falling off' is just a tiny step down.

q: A dhol group of 6 drummers plays a wedding song in 3 minutes. How long would 12 drummers take to play the same song?
note: More drummers make the song louder, not shorter.

q: On a sunny day, one kurta dries on the clothesline in 2 hours. How long do 5 kurtas take, hung side by side?
note: They all dry at the same time in the same sun.

q: If a red house is made of red bricks and a blue house of blue bricks, what is a greenhouse made of?
note: A greenhouse gets its name from the plants grown inside, not the colour of its walls.

q: Say 'roast' five times quickly. What do you put in a toaster?
note: Toast is what comes out; bread is what goes in.

q: Where can you add 2 to 11 and get 1?
note: Two hours after 11 o'clock, a clock shows 1.

q: What is wrong with this sentence: 'I love chai in the the morning'?
note: Our brains tend to skip a repeated small word when reading quickly.

q: How many words are there in this question?
note: How, many, words, are, there, in, this, question: eight.

q: Two friends play five games of chess. Each wins three games, and none are drawn. How?
options: A win on time counts double
note: Each played someone else, so both could win three of their five games.

q: A dealer offers you a coin stamped '250 BC'. How can you tell instantly that it's fake?
a: Nobody in 250 BC knew it was 'BC'
options: Nobody in 250 BC knew it was 'BC'
Dates were always written in words
note: Counting years backwards towards a future date only began centuries later.

q: A square tabletop has 4 corners. You saw off one corner with a short straight cut that touches no other corner. How many corners now?
note: The cut removes one corner but creates two new ones, one at each end of the cut.

q: A farmer has 5 haystacks in one field and 4 in another. He piles them all together in a third field. How many haystacks does he have?
note: Pile nine haystacks together and you get one very big haystack.

q: A ₹10 coin sits inside an empty glass jar sealed with a cork. How can you get the coin out without pulling the cork out or breaking the jar?
a: Push the cork into the jar
options: Shake it out through the cork
Push the cork into the jar
note: The cork never comes out of the jar; it just ends up inside it.

q: Before a cricket match, the visiting captain calls 'heads' and loses the toss. Which way did the coin land?
note: Calling heads and losing can only mean the coin showed tails.

q: Add one letter to IX to make it six.
note: Put an S in front of IX and it spells SIX.

q: How can half of twelve be seven?
a: Cut the Roman numeral XII in half across the middle
options: Cut the Roman numeral XII in half across the middle
note: Slice XII horizontally and the top half reads VII.

q: Write in figures: eleven thousand, eleven hundred and eleven.
alt: Twelve thousand one hundred and eleven

q: Players of Team A score three goals in a football match, yet Team A loses 2-1, with no penalty shootout. How?
a: Two of their goals were own goals
options: Two goals came after the final whistle
Team B was given bonus goals
Two of their goals were own goals
note: Own goals count for the other side, so Team B got 2 and Team A got 1.

q: Multiply together every digit on a phone keypad. What do you get?
note: The keypad includes a 0, and anything multiplied by zero is zero.

q: Work out (x - a)(x - b)(x - c) ... (x - z), with one bracket for each letter from a to z.
note: One of the brackets is (x - x), which is zero, so the whole product is zero.

q: Which clock shows the right time more often: one that has stopped, or one that loses a minute every day?
note: A stopped clock is right twice a day; one losing a minute daily is right once in 720 days.

q: A cow gives 6 litres of milk a day. How many litres does a bullock give?
note: A bullock is male, and only females give milk.

q: It's pouring in Mumbai at midnight. Will there be bright sunshine 72 hours later?
a: No, it will be midnight again
options: No, it will be midnight again
note: 72 hours is exactly three days, so it will be midnight again.

q: A bus starts empty. At stop 1, 8 people get on. At stop 2, 3 get off and 5 get on. At stop 3, 6 get off and 2 get on. How many stops did the bus make?
note: The passenger numbers are a distraction; the question was about stops.

q: Counting upwards in English words (one, two, three...), what is the first number whose name contains the letter B?
note: No number name contains a B until you reach 1,000,000,000.

q: Which number from one to a hundred, spelled out in English, has its letters in A-to-Z order?
note: F, O, R, T, Y: each letter comes later in A to Z than the one before it.

q: Rearrange the letters of DORMITORY into two words that describe it.
note: D-O-R-M-I-T-O-R-Y uses exactly the letters of 'dirty room'.

q: Rohit stands behind Kavya while Kavya stands behind Rohit, at the same time. How?
options: One is on the floor above
note: Back to back, each one is behind the other.

q: A car's distance meter shows 72927 km, a palindrome. Two hours later it shows the next palindrome. What was the car's average speed, in km/h?
note: The next palindrome is 73037, which is 110 km later: 110 ÷ 2 = 55.

q: Which gives you more pizza: one 12-inch pizza, or two 8-inch pizzas of the same thickness?
note: Area grows with the square: 12² = 144, but 8² + 8² is only 128.

q: The digits 0 to 9 used worldwide are often credited to the Arabs. In which country did the system actually begin?
note: Arab scholars carried the Indian system westward, so later readers credited them.

q: In which country was the board game Chinese checkers invented?
note: It began in the 1890s as 'Stern-Halma'; the Chinese name came from American marketing.

q: In which country was the Hawaiian pizza invented?
note: A Greek-born cook, Sam Panopoulos, created it at his restaurant in 1962.

q: Roughly how long is 1,000,000,000 seconds?
note: 1,000,000 seconds is under 12 days, but 1,000,000,000 seconds is almost 32 years.

q: Which common English word, spelled backwards, gives 'stressed'?
note: S-T-R-E-S-S-E-D reversed reads D-E-S-S-E-R-T-S.

q: Why do you always find a lost thing in the last place you look?
a: Because you stop looking once you find it
options: Because you stop looking once you find it
Because you search in the wrong order
Because things hide in odd places
note: Nobody keeps searching after finding it, so wherever it turns up is the last place.

q: What was the name of the ship Columbus sailed to Australia?
note: Columbus never went near it; Europeans first reached Australia in the 1600s.

q: Four friends share one small raincoat on a 2 km walk, yet none of them gets wet. How?
note: Nobody mentioned rain; the raincoat was just along for the walk.

q: A flight from Delhi to Mumbai takes 1 hour 20 minutes, but the return flight takes 80 minutes, with identical winds. Why the difference?
a: There's no difference, 80 minutes is 1 hour 20
options: There's no difference, 80 minutes is 1 hour 20
note: 1 hour 20 minutes and 80 minutes are exactly the same length of time.

q: Can you name a number whose double is smaller than the number itself?
options: No, doubling always makes it bigger
note: Double −3 and you get −6, which is smaller than −3.

q: A car climbs a 1 km hill at 30 km/h. How fast must it come down the 1 km other side to average 60 km/h for the whole 2 km?
a: Impossible, no speed is fast enough
options: Impossible, no speed is fast enough
note: Averaging 60 km/h over 2 km allows 120 seconds, and the climb already used all of them.

q: In a normal cricket match, how many players from both teams are on the field at once?
note: The whole fielding side plus the two batters; the rest of the batting team waits off the field.

q: During play, how many stumps are there on a cricket field?
note: There are three stumps at each end of the pitch.

q: An hourglass holds exactly 60 minutes of sand. After 45 minutes, you flip it over. How many minutes after the flip until the top is empty?
note: Flipping it puts the 45 minutes of fallen sand on top, and that takes 45 minutes to fall.

q: Which common four-letter word becomes 'evil' when written backwards?
note: L-I-V-E reversed is E-V-I-L.

q: You're standing exactly at the North Pole. Whichever way you face, which direction are you looking?
note: From the North Pole, every direction along the ground points south.

q: Which weighs more: 100 grams of sugar or 0.1 kg of salt?
note: 0.1 kg is exactly 100 grams.

q: A lump of ice floats in a glass of water filled right to the brim. When the ice melts, what happens?
a: The water level stays the same
options: The water level stays the same
It overflows only if the ice is large
note: Floating ice pushes aside exactly its own weight of water, which is exactly what it turns into.

q: You're in a boat on a small pond, holding a heavy stone. You drop the stone overboard and it sinks. What happens to the pond's water level?
note: In the boat, the stone displaced its weight in water; on the bottom, only its smaller volume.

q: What is the fourth word in this question?
note: What, is, the, fourth: the answer was hiding in plain sight.

q: A ping-pong ball falls into a narrow pipe fixed upright in the ground. How do you get it out without damaging the pipe?
a: Pour water in so it floats up
options: Pour water in so it floats up
note: A ping-pong ball is light and hollow, so water lifts it to the top.

q: A basket holds 5 mangoes. How can you give 5 friends one mango each and still leave one mango in the basket?
a: Give the last friend the basket with the mango
options: Give the last friend the basket with the mango
note: The fifth friend gets a mango that is still sitting in the basket.

q: A shop sells chocolates at ₹10 each with 'Buy 3, get 1 free'. How much do 8 chocolates cost?
note: Pay for 6 and you get 2 free, which makes 8 chocolates for ₹60.

q: Which is bigger: 99% of 100 or 100% of 99?
note: Both are 99: x% of y always equals y% of x.

q: In a closed car, a toy airship filled with lighter-than-air gas floats freely. When the car speeds up, which way does the airship move relative to the car?
note: Air piles up at the back of the car and buoys the lighter airship forward.

q: A farmer walks his 10 cows and 20 hens to the market. How many feet are walking to the market?
note: 40 cow feet plus 40 hen feet, plus the farmer's own two.

q: Two trains 100 km apart head towards each other at 50 km/h each. A fly zips back and forth between them at 100 km/h until they meet. How far does the fly travel?
note: The trains meet after exactly 1 hour, and the fly flies at 100 km/h all that time.

q: You roll one ₹5 coin all the way around another identical ₹5 coin without slipping. How many full turns does the moving coin make?
note: Going around the other coin adds one extra turn on top of the distance rolled.

q: An exam ends at 12:00 by the correct time. The hall clock is 10 minutes fast and shows 11:30. How much time is really left?
note: The clock is 10 minutes ahead, so the real time is 11:20, leaving 40 minutes.

q: What is the last letter of 'the last letter'?
note: The phrase 'the last letter' itself ends in R.

q: Rearrange the letters of ELEVEN PLUS TWO to make another sum.
note: Both phrases use the same 13 letters, and both add up to 13.

q: Tossing a fair coin five times, which result is more likely: HHHHH or HTHHT?
options: It depends on the first toss
note: Every exact sequence of five fair tosses has the same 1-in-32 chance.

q: A kirana shop's sign says: 'Credit given only to customers over 90 who come with their parents.' What does it really mean?
note: A 90-year-old shopping with their parents is almost impossible, so nobody qualifies.

q: Which English word is wrong if you pronounce it right, and right if you pronounce it wrong?
note: Say 'wrong' correctly and you've said 'wrong'; that is the whole joke.

q: What 7-letter English word becomes longer when you remove its third letter?
note: Take the U out of 'lounger' and you're left with 'longer'.

q: Three switches outside a closed room work three old filament bulbs inside. You may enter only once. How can you tell which switch works which bulb?
a: Switch one on a while, turn it off, switch another on, then feel
options: Switch one on a while, turn it off, switch another on, then feel
Switch all on and count the lit bulbs
Flick each switch and listen for clicks
It can't be done in one visit
note: The lit bulb is the second switch, the warm dark one the first, the cold one the third.

q: A Chennai bus conductor gives a ticket to everyone else on board except one person, yet nobody is travelling free. Who is it?
note: The driver is working, not travelling as a passenger, so needs no ticket.
